dominant_breach: state/local pension promises can protect worker wealth while shifting underfunding, private-market fee drag, valuation lag, illiquidity, capital-call pressure, contribution spikes, benefit-tier conflicts, and service crowdout to taxpayers, workers, retirees, and residents
fastest_washout: aggregate funded ratios and strong headline private-equity returns wash out when plan-level assumptions, net-of-fee reporting, liquidity/cash-flow needs, legal priority, local tax capacity, and service incidence are not scored together

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: State/local pension promises are public claim-security and local-service-capacity claims; active scoring now also requires private-market fee, valuation, liquidity, capital-call, and contrary-performance evidence before treating aggregate assets as comfort.

public_pension_funding_risk.note: Census data, Pew funding/fee evidence, Public Plans Data, S&P current-risk framing, and AIC contrary performance claims show that aggregate assets are not enough; funded status, contribution discipline, net-of-fee results, valuation lag, and liquidity must be stress-tested.

pension_assumption_stress_testing.note: Return assumptions and demographic/salary/longevity misses directly change contribution needs and intergenerational burden. Rev0368 adds private-market lockup, valuation, capital-call, and fee-disclosure stress as a noncertifying acceptance test.

state_local_intergovernmental_burden_shi.note: Local services, taxes, state aid, future residents, and new tiers can absorb pension repair when plans under-amortize, markets underperform, or private-market cash-flow/valuation lags hide contribution pressure.

public_backstop_seniority_waterfall.note: The case must show whether retirees, bondholders, current workers, taxpayers, service users, future residents, and asset managers/GP fee claims are senior during stress; manager fees and carried interest cannot remain outside the waterfall.

proof_debt: plan-level funded ratios, assets, liabilities, cash flow, and actuarial assumptions using Census/Pew/NASRA/plan disclosures
investment-return assumption sensitivity and contribution shock under market stress
legal protection map for retirees, current workers, new tiers, bondholders, and local service users
service-cut, tax, user-fee, wage, and infrastructure crowdout incidence by locality and income class
pension-obligation-bond, amortization, COLA, tier, and state-aid burden-shift pathways
private-market fee, carried-interest, valuation-lag, capital-call, and liquidity-stress evidence by plan and vintage
contrary net-of-fee return evidence and survivorship/selection/method limits, including industry-side claims, before condemning or certifying private markets

gate_20_public_balance_sheet.why: Comfort certification is blocked until state/local pension funding is scored at plan/locality level with legal priority, assumption stress, contribution discipline, service crowdout, taxpayer/worker/retiree incidence, and private-market fee/liquidity/valuation/net-return evidence.

evidence_debt_register.question: state/local pension asset, membership, benefit-payment, and contribution perimeter
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use Census ASPP, Pew, and plan disclosures to bind assets, participants, contributions, benefits, and actuarial data to the case.

evidence_debt_register.question: return-assumption and market-stress sensitivity
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Stress-test plan funding and contributions under lower returns, market drawdowns, salary/longevity misses, and amortization policy.

evidence_debt_register.question: legal seniority of retirees, workers, bondholders, service users, and taxpayers
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Map constitutional/statutory protections, bankruptcy constraints, COLA/tier rules, debt covenants, and local service obligations.

evidence_debt_register.question: local public-service and tax incidence
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Translate required contribution increases or underfunding into school, infrastructure, public safety, tax, user-fee, and wage channels by locality.

evidence_debt_register.question: private-market fee, liquidity, valuation, and net-of-fee reporting waterfall
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Bind plan-level private equity/private debt commitments, unfunded commitments, capital calls, distributions, management fees, carried interest, performance fees, valuation policy, NAV lag, continuation-vehicle exposure, redemption/secondary-sale limits, and audited net-of-fee returns.

20A_debt_interest_capacity.question: Do debt service and maturity/interest risks crowd out floors, services, enforcement, public investment, or countercyclical repair?
20A_debt_interest_capacity.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20B_claim_security.question: Are social-insurance, pension, health, disability, care, or public-benefit promises financed and legally durable enough to count as wealth substitutes?
20B_claim_security.finding: Public-pension claim security varies by plan and law; underfunding, fee drag, private-market valuation delay, and liquidity/capital-call stress can compress services or worker claims.

20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.question: Are guarantees, insurance funds, credit programs, SOEs, PPPs, disaster obligations, and legal claims disclosed and stress-tested?
20C_contingent_liabilities_guarantees.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20D_crisis_backstop_governance.question: Who is rescued under stress, under what terms, with what haircut, condition, sunset, and report?
20D_crisis_backstop_governance.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20E_public_upside_recovery.question: Does the public receive warrants, equity, fees, clawbacks, senior claims, recoveries, or other upside when it absorbs downside?
20E_public_upside_recovery.finding: When public pension beneficiaries and taxpayers bear private-market fee, liquidity, and valuation risk, certification requires evidence of net-of-fee public value, clawbacks, fee offsets, governance rights, transparency, and downside sharing rather than assumed manager upside.

20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.question: Are remittance losses, deferred assets, interest-on-reserves distribution, facilities, and asset-price stabilization effects visible?
20F_central_bank_quasi_fiscal_visibility.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.question: Are public assets rule-bound, professionally managed, protected from raiding, and linked to ordinary claimants?
20G_public_asset_sovereign_wealth_govern.finding: This subgate is not a material live channel in this case.

20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.question: Does repair fall on younger cohorts, renters, disabled claimants, caregivers, migrants, municipalities, or future taxpayers?
20H_generational_intergovernmental_incid.finding: Local service users, younger workers, new tiers, taxpayers, and future residents can bear amortization, contribution, liquidity, and fee/valuation repair pressure.

public_balance_sheet_register.exposure_name: U.S. state/local defined-benefit pension promises, assumption risk, contribution discipline, and local-service incidence
public_balance_sheet_register.legal_authority: State constitutions/statutes, pension-plan contracts, collective-bargaining arrangements, actuarial funding policy, GASB disclosures, local budget law, and bankruptcy/municipal distress constraints
public_balance_sheet_register.claimant_perimeter: Retirees, current public workers, new-tier workers, taxpayers, local service users, municipal bondholders, state aid providers, public employers, and future residents
public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: Plan-specific accrued liabilities and unfunded actuarial liabilities plus contribution-shock, COLA, pension-obligation-bond, amortization-risk, private-market unfunded-commitment/capital-call, fee-drag, liquidity, and valuation-lag exposure.
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Actuarial contribution gap, benefit-tier erosion, service crowdout, tax/user-fee increases, wage restraint, state-aid shift, or hidden fee/valuation loss under market/demographic/assumption/liquidity stress.
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: Investment underperformance or demographic/salary/longevity misses raise required contributions while local tax bases and service needs are constrained, forcing priority conflicts among retirees, workers, bondholders, taxpayers, and residents.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: Trust assets, employer contributions, employee contributions, taxes, service cuts, benefit/tier reforms, COLA changes, debt issuance, state aid, and investment returns.
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Loss sharing depends on legal protection and plan design; the case must prevent asymmetric protection of high-benefit claims while low-wage workers, services, and future residents absorb repair.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Contribution discipline, conservative assumptions, transparent net-of-fee reporting, clawback/fee-offset rights, anti-spiking controls, amortization repair, state-aid conditions, governance reforms, and manager accountability that preserve both retiree claims and public services.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Protect low-wage public workers, retirees with limited outside wealth, essential local services, low-income taxpayers, and future workers before bondholder priority, high-benefit/high-income claimant priority, or private manager fee claims become absolute.
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Annual actuarial/GASB/Census/Pew refresh; immediate review after major market drawdown, COLA/tier law change, pension-obligation bond issuance, bankruptcy/distress filing, or state-aid intervention.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: low-wealth retirees and low-wage current public workers
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Should be protected against poverty and broken earned claims, but protection must be distribution-aware.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Legal protection may seniorize pension checks over service expansion.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: essential local service users and low-income taxpayers
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Must not become the silent residual claimant through service cuts, regressive fees, or local tax stress.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Debt covenants may compete with pension and service claims.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: bondholders, high-benefit claimants, and pension-obligation-bond structures
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Need transparent legal priority and loss sharing; should not outrank ordinary claimant protection by default.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Contribution increases, wage restraint, or service cuts can become the shock absorber.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: asset managers, GP fee/carry claims, consultants, and private-market intermediaries
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Must be made explicit; fee and carried-interest claims should not be invisible senior claims on worker/taxpayer-funded trust assets.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Net-of-fee reporting, clawbacks, fee offsets, valuation policy, and liquidity/capital-call terms are acceptance-test records.

seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Cannot inherit under-amortization, reduced tiers, weak services, and deferred repair without explicit incidence scoring.
